title: Can someone help me figure out custom tile sizes?

posts.author: GuardianofRidgewood
posts.body: I was thinking of making my own tiles and tilesets just to make my game look a bit better and so I'm not using the same layouts for everything. I just don't know how big things need to be. I read the asset standards in the help section like I found in another post, but I'm having a hard time understanding it fully. From what I understand MZ supports 16x16, 24x24, 32x32, and 48x48, right? But then what is this 512x384 stuff it's talking about in the image attached? Can someone just give me a clear, simple to understand answer on this? If I want to make my own tiles for the inside of a house for instance, how big should I make the single tile? Like is there a standard or recommended size? Any help would be appreciated.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body: That would be the size of the entire sheet I would think.

posts.author: Kes
posts.body:
If you are using MZ, then probably the best tile size is 48x48.  But that is a tile.  An individual object could take up several tiles, as you can see from the default assets.  You use as many tiles for each object as you need.
Each tile sheet is a specific size.  No variation allowed.  If that means a particular sheet is half empty, so be it.  Again, look at the defaults.  The tile sheets that fit in slots B-E are all 768x768.  The tile sheets on the A tab vary, and you will need to check each one.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Have you spent time making maps and practice games with RPG Maker before trying to customize it? It makes sense to be familiar with how everything works and what the terminology is before changing things.
As
@SGHarlekin
says, you appear to be confusing yourself between "a tile" and "the tileset" which consists of several "tilesheets" with many individual tiles on each.
Just look at it in the TIlesets tab of the database, and at the actual tilesheets in the img\tilesets folder of your project.
This is also all clear if you read the other portions of the instructions that have to do with tilesheets.
etc.

posts.author: GuardianofRidgewood
posts.body: Thank you everyone for replying. I figured it out after reading the replies and I'm happy to say that I was able to successfully add my first custom tileset to my project. It's not good by any means, but I proved that I can do it.
